observation_summary: Calling a real method on an interface mock caused a NullPointerException or NoSuchMethodError because the system attempted to invoke a method that does not exist on an interface.
reasoning_summary: The fix adds a guard clause (an 'if' statement) to check if the method being called belongs to an interface. If it does, it throws a descriptive exception instead of proceeding with the invalid invocation. This is a classic missing validation check.
evidence_used: The failing tests indicate that the system was attempting to call real methods on interfaces, which is an invalid operation.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: The core issue is not the logic of the invocation itself, but the lack of a guard to prevent an invalid operation on an interface.
This is a local procedural check, not a design-level capability gap.
